name: Liberty spikes

card.summary: A tall punk hairstyle of thick, upright hair spikes, worn for a bold, high-impact silhouette and a statement look.
card.note: Strong-hold styling products can be hard on hair and scalp with frequent use.

quick.overview:
Liberty spikes are a punk hairstyle made of several thick, upright spikes that radiate from the scalp, named for their resemblance to the crown of the Statue of Liberty. They are an eye-catching way to add height and drama to the head.

The look emerged in the punk subculture and is associated with individuality and nonconformity, and it is usually dyed in bold colours or black.
quick.how: Hair is teased at the roots for volume, then shaped into pointed spikes with strong-hold products such as hairspray or gel; styling is described as taking significant time. Some wearers dye the hair for added impact.
quick.risks: Frequent teasing, bleaching and strong-hold products can leave hair dry or brittle, and the style draws a lot of attention in conservative workplaces. Grokipedia reports sessions can take over an hour.

lead: Liberty spikes are a punk hairstyle in which hair is shaped into multiple thick, upright spikes, named for the spikes of the Statue of Liberty's crown [1]. Wearers typically tease the roots for volume and set the spikes with strong-hold products, sometimes adding vivid dye [1].
People wear them as a deliberate, high-impact statement: the spikes add height and a dramatic silhouette. In punk, the look signals rebellion and individuality [1].

Punk hair in the early 1970s was cropped and messy; by the 1980s it was shaved, spiked, or cut as a crew cut or Mohawk, with tall mohawks and brightly coloured spikes more extreme than the 1970s styles [2]. Liberty spikes later appear in anarcho-punk and street punk and in a 2010s pop-punk revival [2].

chain: Tease and set hair into tall spikes
Adds height and a bold silhouette
angle.text: Liberty spikes change the whole shape of the head and are a visible expression of punk identity. The result is a dramatic, instantly recognisable hairstyle.

paras: The style consists of thick spikes radiating from the scalp, with hair teased at the roots and shaped with strong-hold products [1].

Grokipedia places the emergence of liberty spikes in the British punk scene of the late 1970s, growing taller through the 1980s [1]. Wikipedia's punk fashion article credits Richard Hell with helping popularise the spiked look, and notes liberty spikes among later anarcho-punk and street punk styles [2].
Beyond punk the look has influenced goth styling, where the spikes are often dyed black [1].

timeline.event: Spiked hair becomes part of the punk look [2].
Tall mohawks and brightly coloured spikes become more extreme [2].
Liberty spikes return in pop punk alongside wide mohawks [2].
